misconceptions.title: Subtracts instead of dividing
misconceptions.description: Takes one amount away from the other when the question asks how many groups fit into a total.
misconceptions.feedback: Close. You took one amount away from the other once. The question asks how many times the smaller amount fits into the total, and that is a division.

misconceptions.title: Adds instead of dividing
misconceptions.description: Adds the two amounts when the question asks how many groups fit into a total.
misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. You added the two amounts, so your answer is bigger than the total. Ask how many groups of the smaller amount make the total. That is a division.

misconceptions.title: Multiplies instead of dividing
misconceptions.description: Multiplies the two amounts when the question asks how many groups fit into a total.
misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. Multiplying made your answer far bigger than the total. When you want how many groups fit into a total, divide the total by the size of one group.

misconceptions.title: Divides top and bottom by different numbers
misconceptions.description: Simplifies by dividing the numerator and the denominator by different numbers, which changes the value of the fraction.
misconceptions.feedback: Close. You divided the top and the bottom by different numbers, and that changes the fraction's value. Divide both by the same common factor.

misconceptions.title: Stops before lowest terms
misconceptions.description: Divides by a common factor that is not the HCF, so the fraction is equivalent but not fully simplified.
misconceptions.feedback: Right value, not finished. The top and the bottom still share a factor. Divide both by their highest common factor to reach lowest terms.

misconceptions.title: Adds tops and adds bottoms
misconceptions.description: Adds numerators together and denominators together, so 1/2 + 1/3 becomes 2/5.
misconceptions.feedback: Close. You added the tops and added the bottoms. Halves and thirds are different sized pieces, so change them to the same denominator before you add.

misconceptions.title: Adds tops, multiplies bottoms
misconceptions.description: Multiplies the denominators to get a common denominator but adds the numerators unchanged, so 1/2 + 1/3 becomes 2/6.
misconceptions.feedback: Close. You found a common denominator but left the tops as they were. When the bottom of a fraction is multiplied, the top must be multiplied by the same number.

misconceptions.title: Finds one part and stops
misconceptions.description: Divides by the denominator to find one part but does not multiply by the numerator.
misconceptions.feedback: Halfway there. You found one part. The question asks for more than one part, so multiply by the top number as well.

misconceptions.title: Orders the wrong way round
misconceptions.description: Puts the values in descending order when the question asks for ascending, or the reverse.
misconceptions.feedback: Your order is right but reversed. Ascending means smallest first, climbing up.

misconceptions.title: Judges size by the denominator alone
misconceptions.description: Treats the fraction with the bigger denominator as always the smaller one, ignoring the numerator.
misconceptions.feedback: Close. A bigger denominator means smaller pieces, but the top number counts how many pieces you have. Compare the fractions over a common denominator.

misconceptions.title: Cuts a recurring decimal short
misconceptions.description: Converts a fraction such as 2/3 to 0.6 instead of 0.666..., which makes it look smaller than it is.
misconceptions.feedback: Close. One of these fractions is a recurring decimal, and cutting it short made it look smaller than it is. Keep more decimal places, or compare over a common denominator.

misconceptions.title: Multiplies instead of dividing a fraction
misconceptions.description: Multiplies the fraction by the whole number when the question asks to divide.
misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. You multiplied instead of dividing. Sharing a fraction into more parts makes each part smaller, not bigger.

misconceptions.title: Divides the wrong way round
misconceptions.description: Divides the second number by the first, for example works out 4 ÷ 2/3 instead of 2/3 ÷ 4.
misconceptions.feedback: Close. You divided the second number by the first. Order matters in division: the first number is the one being shared out.

misconceptions.title: No misconception named yet
misconceptions.description: Placeholder for a distractor nobody has explained yet. Name the error behind it or replace the distractor.
misconceptions.feedback: Not quite. Open a hint and try again.
